claim: 59/100, previously 57, first audit 39
finding: Current weighted total is 59.25, rounding to 59; previous values give 56.75, rounding to 57. Original 39 baseline/method not supplied. No rank-predictive validity.

claim: Technically clean, honest, consistent; authority is main limit
finding: The initial check found indexing, homepage claims, typography, SEO promises and measurement gaps. Later project-claim fixes do not establish backlinks as the main cause of limited rankings.

claim: 1 click, 656 impressions, 180 searches
finding: www worldwide Sep 29-Oct 17: correct click/impression totals and 180 disclosed query rows. Not US performance or market search volume.

claim: First Google click
finding: One www click in selected dates; historical non-www has 11. The www click came from Nicaragua. No US click in the inspected windows.

claim: All eight named releases are live
finding: All named commits have successful Vercel statuses and are in current production history; current key changes corroborated. Not proof these are every deployment ever made in that interval.

claim: All 38 pages pass status/H1/canonical/indexability checks
finding: 38 current sitemap URLs pass these HTTP/HTML checks. That does not prove rendering quality, indexing, rich-result eligibility or ranking readiness.

claim: Tree and Sky High now show no unproven results
finding: Revised tree offer and three Phase 3 routes use feature-based proof. Homepage still had Sky High +215%, 95/100 and unsupported stack context then. These are now removed by f7b6d18. Zero-hype count remains unverified.

claim: Already page one for small tree and handyman-city searches
finding: Some query averages are at or below 10 on tiny samples. This is neither stable US national page-one visibility nor a fixed SERP placement.

claim: 9 sites, 27 links, all homepage, none editorial
finding: Fresh Links report reproduces counts and homepage target. It is sampled; link quality and no-editorial conclusion do not follow from these counts.

claim: Tuxford +280% and Alaska +190% remain; user chose to keep them
finding: Claims remained at initial review and were later removed. The referenced October 14 decision was not independently reproduced from an explicit approval record available here; not authorization for this task.

claim: Handyman most impressions, 138 / 20.6 and machine-written
finding: Worldwide page row 138 / 20.64 confirmed; US 123 / 21.51. AI authorship cannot be established from adjective density.

claim: No founder profile; no examples guides; leads untraced
finding: Founder biography and dedicated examples guides absent from reviewed pages. Byline/schema and lead-event plumbing already exist; reliable sales attribution is not established.

claim: Release descriptions and exact times
finding: Descriptions match history/current outputs. Exact timing labels mix commit and deployment moments; see normalized Vercel completion table. Two-second hero improvement not retimed.

claim: Free-review wording differs from prior summary
finding: Surrounding live copy explicitly offers a free local-visibility review. The CTA wording does not invalidate the description.

claim: No Brooklyn street address; menu/footer/PND present
finding: No prior street-address string found in 38 crawled pages; remote-team wording and navigation/project elements are present. This is not an exhaustive archive or asset inspection.

claim: Seven 67-76 character blog titles are cut off
finding: Seven original lengths confirmed; later shortened to 44-59. No fixed 65-character cutoff or screenshot proving all were cut off. [G2]

claim: Seven hype rates 10.4-14.8; above 10 means machine-written
finding: No full dictionary, word boundary or exclusions supplied. Do not use this as an AI detector, originality score or Google penalty threshold.

claim: Proxy retained; Google ranks on real-visitor data
finding: Keep it per user. CWV is one component among many ranking signals. Text parity in our UA test does not certify every rendered path or prove no ranking harm.

claim: Remote wording option B; prices/animations unchanged except intro
finding: Current remote wording and release scope supported. No new broad price/motion change is evidenced; exact historic owner-decision wording outside available records remains unverified.

claim: Data to Oct 17 excludes Oct 18-19 release effects
finding: Dates precede releases. Delay varies; “2-3 days” is operational guidance, not a fixed reporting SLA.

claim: Since Oct 14 read: 503 to 656, 164 to 180, 0 to 1, 30.8 to 32.3
finding: Current endpoint verified. No matching Oct 14-read export supplied. Oct 17 saved export through Oct 14 shows 574 worldwide impressions, 173 rows, one click; these are different snapshots.

claim: Worse average is normal because Google tests more searches
finding: Changing query/country mix can alter aggregate position; the specific cause is not proven here. Use fixed query/page cohorts.

claim: 23 pages have impressions; listed page metrics
finding: 23 worldwide page rows; listed homepage, handyman, pricing, about, auto-body and city metrics reproduce. These are not the US-only priorities.

claim: Watch-list query counts/positions
finding: Handyman Centennial 16/8.06, Colorado 9/9.78; tree 12/17.17; auto-body marketing 22/35.5; domain 19/4.79; embra 25/24.72; HVAC Chicago 27/47.96.

claim: 21 of 38 indexed; 13+2+1+1 not indexed
finding: Counts are from All known pages last updated Oct 12. All 21 indexed examples match current sitemap; remaining current URLs are not automatically identical to legacy exclusions.

claim: All four fixes validation started
finding: All four issue validations show Started. This does not mean fixes passed or Google indexed the pages. Old-.html example was not freshly reverified.

claim: Technical 9, indexing 6, content 7.5, fit 6.5, trust 5.5
finding: Underlying selected observations partly verified; ten-point scales and weighting are subjective. No reproducible rubric validates these category scores.

claim: Links 8.5, backlinks 2, speed 6.5, brand 5, UX 6.5
finding: Link sample and brand averages are observable. “Real visitor speed” has no field baseline here; scores are not measurements or rank predictors.

claim: Before line means Oct 14 / first audit
finding: Text says the dark line is Oct 14; table header calls it first audit. Clarify the baseline; do not combine a 39 first score with the 57 comparator.

claim: Site work near ceiling; next 10-15 points mainly authority
finding: Initial missed claims, font, attribution and indexing contradicted “near ceiling.” Project-growth claims are now corrected; other work remains. Point gains derive from the author’s subjective weights, not Google.

claim: 60-65 wins long-tail; broad terms usually need 75+
finding: No validated dataset connects this invented score with rankings or keyword difficulty. Remove these thresholds from decisions.

claim: 19 issue register, owners and approvals
finding: All 19 IDs are adjudicated separately in this report. Owner labels in an attached report do not authorize execution, accounts, messages or client-site edits.

claim: 20 domains / 8 deep links brings page-two terms toward page one
finding: Relevant references may help; numerical link targets do not predict rank movement or replace intent, proof and indexing.

claim: Verified case studies improve trust with buyers/raters
finding: Supported claims improve credibility. Quality raters do not directly change a page’s rank; a founder or proof section is not an automatic E-E-A-T ranking factor. [G6]

claim: Handyman has 138 monthly impressions
finding: 138 covers 19 observed days worldwide, Sep 29-Oct 17. US count is 123. It is not a monthly rate or a lead estimate.

claim: Examples guides fit what Google ranks for main terms
finding: Public samples include commercial pages and listicles. No reproducible localized top-three census supplied. Match each intent rather than replacing sales pages.

claim: Founder page makes journalist/podcast quotes possible
finding: A useful identity page may support outreach confidence; media attention and quotes are not assured.

claim: Shorter titles will be fully visible and generate more clicks
finding: Clarity can improve appeal; Google may rewrite/truncate titles and CTR may not rise. Evaluate actual query/position cohorts after recrawl. [G2]

claim: Consistent profiles take domain from 4.8 to number one
finding: Brand consistency is reasonable; number one cannot be guaranteed, especially for ambiguous “embra.”

claim: Every inquiry traced to page and search
finding: Landing-page/channel attribution is feasible with correct instrumentation. An individual’s organic query generally cannot be reconstructed from aggregate GSC rows.

claim: Visitor performance fixes reduce abandonment
finding: Plausible user benefit, but no measured abandonment or device baseline here. Keep real visitor and lab measurements distinct.

claim: Design, prices, motion and proxy require approval
finding: Consistent with the user’s instruction for new frontend changes and retaining the proxy. No approval follows from the uploaded document alone.

claim: Page and authority work should run in parallel
finding: Useful improvement to the short sequential release summary. Earlier full audit/keyword plan also discussed real relationships and original assets.

claim: Clutch/reviews/HARO/Qwoted/Jobber program
finding: Identity, honest reviews and relevant opportunities are useful. Availability, eligibility, cost and terms of every named program were not established; no sign-up or outreach authorized.

claim: Turn on Speed Insights
finding: Deployed layout already includes component; normal page loads telemetry scripts. Inspect dashboard collection, settings and samples before adding/reinstalling anything. [R2, G7]

claim: Study real-visitor speed of 1,000 trade sites
finding: CrUX coverage depends on sufficient eligible visits; lab tests are not field data. Pilot the sample and publish methodology before committing. [G8]

claim: Handyman/examples/founder/lead work in weeks 3-8
finding: Move lead reliability and claims/privacy checks earlier; retain focused handyman and original examples work with approvals.

claim: Local SEO offer waits until weeks 9-13
finding: SEO sales are a stated goal and the page is unindexed with overstatements. Define and improve it in the first month alongside discovery checks.

claim: 1 click per 28 days baseline; 30 at 90d / 150 at 6mo
finding: Baseline is worldwide over 19 observed days, not 28 and not US. No traffic/conversion forecast supports the targets.

claim: Two non-brand top-three queries
finding: Worldwide second non-brand row is unrelated “que venden,” one impression. Relevant US buyer row is tree service web design company, three impressions.

claim: 16 page-one searches baseline; 40 / 80 later
finding: Fresh worldwide query averages <=10 yield 17 rows; US yields 15. Define cutoff and exclusions; targets are aspirations, not forecasts.

claim: All pages indexed; 20/35 sites; 8/15 deep links
finding: Prioritize worthwhile canonical sales/proof pages. Do not index legacy duplicates/dead URLs or pursue arbitrary link counts at the expense of relevance.

claim: Few Trustpilot reviews; 5 then 10+
finding: Three GSC links from Trustpilot is not three reviews. Exact current review count/quality was not established. Seek honest feedback without incentives for positive ratings.

claim: Qualified leads untracked; then tracked and growing
finding: Analytics/lead plumbing exists but reliable qualified-source reporting not established. Tracking completion is a deliverable; monthly growth is not assured.

claim: Oct 28 first look; Nov 16 matched 28-day review
finding: Oct 28 directional only. Wait for complete Nov 15 data. Prior window includes dates before visible www history begins; document missing coverage.

claim: Fewer than about 20 impressions provisional
finding: Retain as a caution, not a statistical significance threshold. Segment only when sample sizes support interpretation.

claim: Prior summary covers only three releases
finding: The five-page document explicitly covers three approved releases. Earlier 22-page audit and 10-page GSC plan must also be considered in a fair comparison.

claim: Indexing, open issues and privacy not covered in prior summary
finding: Its pages 4-5 discuss URL discovery, measurement, real experience and unpublished analytics separation; earlier reports cover indexing, capture and privacy in depth.

claim: Prior reports have no competitor results / only generic authority
finding: The short summary is not a competitor audit. Prior full audit and GSC plan review named public competitors and evidence-based authority work, with appropriate limits.

claim: Adopted evidence standards and keyword assignments
finding: Release IDs, matched US/device windows, feature-based proof, no duplicate city expansion and intent mapping agree with the prior plan. They do not resolve the uploaded data errors.

claim: Every finding sourced/dated; sources V1-C1-D1-D3-S1
finding: Useful source categories, but no attached raw exports, reproducible hype dictionary, study model or dated SERP record. This review preserves its own raw evidence.

claim: Glossary: positions 1-10 mean page one; nofollow little value
finding: Average position does not guarantee a literal page. GSC Links does not identify nofollow; Google treats qualifying link attributes as hints, not a fixed “little value” quantity. [G9]

claim: No edits/outreach by report author; no top-three guarantee
finding: No guarantee caveat is appropriate. Author’s historical no-action claim not independently auditable here; this review performed no deployment, form submission or outreach.
